entry.name: MIT 6.S191: Introduction to Deep Learning
entry.note: MIT's annual bootcamp; every January's lectures posted free with labs

reading.cost: All materials are open-sourced to the world for free and are copyrighted under the MIT license.
reading.format: The course is delivered in person at MIT and online, with lectures, slides, and labs open-sourced weekly. MIT students can register for credit or as listeners. The 2026 for-credit version is a 3-unit course graded pass/D/fail based on completion of a project proposal assignment.
reading.summary: MIT 6.S191 is an introductory course on deep learning methods. It covers applications in vision, robotics, medicine, language, game play, and art. Students gain foundational knowledge of deep learning algorithms, practical experience building neural networks, and exposure to large language models and generative AI. The course ends with a project proposal competition with feedback from staff and industry sponsors.
reading.audience: The page says it is for MIT students and non-MIT participants. It is beginner friendly and many registered students come from outside computer science. Listeners are welcome.
reading.prerequisites: The page states that calculus (taking derivatives) and linear algebra (matrix multiplication) are assumed. Experience in Python is helpful but not necessary.
